profile.summary: MirrorDNA is a very small DNA language model, 2.35M parameters for the main model, that learns its own way of splitting DNA into tokens. Its tokenizer is built so that a sequence and its reverse complement, the two strands of the same DNA, are always split into mirror-image pieces, so both strands get the same tokens. It is pretrained on the human genome and fine-tuned for DNA classification and regression tasks, giving features that either ignore strand or keep it, depending on the task.

A research model for DNA sequence classification and regression, mainly with fine-tuning.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: DNA is double-stranded, so the same stretch can be read in either direction as its reverse complement. MirrorDNA learns how to cut a sequence into chunks (its tokens) with a symmetric boundary router built so that a sequence and its reverse complement are always cut into mirror-image chunks, whatever the parameter values. Both strands therefore get the same tokens. Bases pass through an encoder, the router chooses chunk boundaries and a transformer works on the chunks. A decoder produces per-base features at full resolution, from which the model computes its output logits; pretraining is masked language modelling with 15% of bases masked. For downstream tasks the model gives pooled features that do not depend on strand, or orientation-aware features for labels that do, such as promoters or splice sites.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three checkpoints were released with one pretraining recipe: the main MirrorDNA model, a duplex-encoder variant, and a control without the equivariance guarantee that relies on reverse-complement augmentation instead. The repository includes the weights, a numerical test of the equivariance guarantee, a two-minute quick start on a small test data set, and scripts to rerun every pretraining, baseline and analysis step of the paper. A result should name the checkpoint folder or Hugging Face repository and its revision; this page read the repository at commit 9c432fc4 and mirrordna-tiny on Hugging Face at revision 11bedeae.

facts.value: Small DNA language model with a learned, reverse-complement-equivariant tokenizer, pretrained by masked language modelling and used mainly through fine-tuning for sequence classification and regression.

Pretraining: masked language modelling on hg38

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: An encoder over bases (shared-weight convolutional in MirrorDNA, cross-strand gated duplex in MirrorDNA-duplex), a symmetric boundary router that cuts the sequence into chunks, a chunk transformer, a decoder and task heads. The released configurations use width 96, 4 encoder layers, 4 main layers, 2 decoder layers, 4 heads and a target chunk ratio of 4.0.

facts.value: DNA sequences encoded one base per position (A, C, G, T, N as 0 to 4).

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Chunk boundaries (the learned tokenisation), strand-invariant pooled sequence features, and orientation-aware pooled features for strand-dependent labels; after fine-tuning, class predictions on both strands.

run_guide.summary: Install MirrorDNA at a pinned commit, check the equivariance guarantee, and run the quick start, which shows the learned chunks and fine-tunes the bundled model on a small gene-strand data set.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 or 3.11 and PyTorch 2.1 or newer, as the README states. Runs on GPU or CPU; for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs the README gives a CUDA 12.8 PyTorch build.
No downloads beyond pip packages: the weights and the test data set are in the repository.
Code and weights are MIT licensed.

cd MirrorDNA

pip install -r requirements.txt
